note: For a hypothetical n>=2 solution, put d=gcd(a,b,c) and x=a/d,y=b/d,z=c/d. Homogeneity gives 2x^n+3y^n=4z^n and gcd(x,y,z)=1. Modulo 2 forces y even. Since n>=2, y^n is divisible by 4; hence 2x^n is divisible by 4, so x is even. Primitivity then forces z odd.

If n>=3, x,y even make the left side divisible by 8, whereas z odd makes 4z^n congruent to 4 modulo 8. If n=2, write x=2X,y=2Y, giving 2X^2+3Y^2=z^2. Modulo 2 forces Y odd. Since Y,z are odd, their squares are 1 modulo 8, so 2X^2 is 6 modulo 8, impossible because any square is 0 or 1 modulo 4 and hence 2X^2 is 0 or 2 modulo 8. The sole admissible exponent is n=1, witnessed by (a,b,c)=(1,2,2).
